goal: Avoid repeatedly decrypting every original at native inner authority gates while proving held history matches actual registered manifest content and current source-purpose authority.
procedure: Retain the existing full comparison input registration and initial history authorization/recovery to authenticate real encrypted originals and manifest; for each later current check accept only the actual selected policy/custody/registry/permission services; verify exact current scope and service bindings; validate the held typed history and hash every in-memory original; resolve actual committed canonical events and current registered sources/raw references; require every original and parent to be in the exact ordered phase history with causal commit positions earlier than children and the manifest; run actual phase-purpose permission closure checks using only this pass's sampled actual metadata rows; reconstruct the precise flora-comparison-history-manifest-v1 body with case, phase, history hash and ordered event/registration/event hashes using the actual custody writer encoding; require its SHA to equal both actual artifact content_sha256 and canonical manifest event content_digest and durable manifest raw reference; discard sampled readers and freshly fence the artifact, canonical commits and every source registration/raw reference through original services, then check exact current grants after all slower metadata work; return a typed observation or fail closed, never a positive authority cache.
authority: Existing selected source-purpose permission and canonical registered custody remain authoritative. The helper grants no read, approval, external disclosure or model execution and certifies no scientific phase exclusion.
validation: Eleven local tests pass with actual selected comparison custody/source registry/permission implementations, real encrypted initial custody and Ed25519 permission authentication, with controlled SQL/log ports. Tests cover zero private ciphertext/plaintext I/O, reordered history, later-after history presented as before, held plaintext mutation, forged manifest content metadata with plausible outer fields, cross-scope history/policy, source and parent revocation between calls, revocation during the final original's grant lookup, raw-reference mutation during grant work, consent withdrawal during the final uncached raw-reference lookup and wrong policy types. Physical selected-engine execution and the declared comparison latency/resource budget remain separate required gates.
failure_or_lesson: The former inner authority path reread every original while recursively guarding private native proof reads. Outer metadata.history_sha256 alone is not proof of the encrypted manifest body. Reconstruction must bind exact ordered current registration hashes and event hashes to the actual manifest and canonical event content digest. Metadata sampling can reduce duplicate lookups within one pass only; a final original-reader fence is needed after grant traversal. Stored immutable phase content is distinct from current permission and from actual model training exclusion.
notes: No learned artifact or real user data is used. Actual initial ciphertext authentication remains separate; this helper hashes already held bytes and reads metadata only. Controlled SQL/log ports establish method behavior rather than engine durability or deployment performance. The returned typed proof is only a current observation, not authority for later calls. This public-method seed stays in FloRA and is not a linked supervised builder case.
